verses.1: And when it became necessary for us to leave them and go our own way, we rushed towards the Kō. From there, we continued on to the Rhodos. And from there, we went to Pátara.
verses.2: And after finding a ship that could sail to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set off.
verses.3: After we reached Cyprus, we landed there and took control of it. Then we sailed towards Syria. We arrived in Tyre, where the ship was loading with goods.
verses.4: But after they found the disciples, we stayed with them for seven days. This was because they told Paul, through the Spirit, that he should not go to Jerusalem.
verses.5: And when it became necessary for us to spend our days away from home, we would go out as merchants, along with our wives and children, until we reached the outskirts of the city. There, we would stand with our backs to the altar, in a solemn manner.
verses.6: We got on the ship with each other. Then we boarded the ship, while those others went back to their own ships.
verses.7: While we were sailing along from Tyrus to Ptolemais, we stopped at one of our brothers’ homes for a day.
verses.8: At the end of the journey, we went to Caesarea. After entering the house of Philip, the evangelist, we stayed with him for seven days.
verses.9: In this case, there were four virgins who prophesied.
verses.10: After several days passed, a man from the Judean prophet named Hagabus disappeared.
verses.11: And when he came to us and laid the cross of Paul on the ground, he said, “This is what the Holy Spirit says: This man is the one whose cross is here. In Jerusalem, the Jews will accept this and give it to other nations.”
verses.12: When we heard these things, we and the people living there decided not to take him back to Jerusalem.
verses.13: Then Paul said, “What do you cry and mourn over me? For I not only am willing to die for the sake of the name of the Lord Jesus, but I also have a duty to die in Jerusalem.”
verses.14: But we did not persuade him to be quiet, and said, “Let us fulfill the master’s wish.”
verses.15: After these days, we went up to Jerusalem.
verses.16: We also joined our students from Caesarea with us. They brought along with them a Cypriot named Mnason, who was one of our ancient disciples.
verses.17: Because of this, our brothers in Jerusalem treated us with great disrespect.
verses.18: And at that moment, Paul went with us to see Jacob. All the elders also came along with us.
verses.19: And, explaining to them individually, he described what God had done for each of those nations through their service.
verses.20: And those who heard this praised the God. They said to Him, “Brothers, consider how many Jews there are who have believed in Him. And all of them are obedient to His laws.”
verses.21: They also discussed the fact that you teach a doctrine of separation from Moses, regarding all the Jews according to their nations. You say that they should not allow their children to practice those practices or follow those customs.
verses.22: What is it then? After all, they will hear that you’ve given up.
verses.23: So, let us tell you what we mean by this. Among us, there are four men who have no desire for anything on their own.
verses.24: By taking them along with you, you will be treated with respect and given money to help them pay for their expenses. In this way, everyone will realize that what they have heard about you is not true at all. Instead, they will understand that you simply follow the rules.
verses.25: As for those nations that have been conquered, we have sent judges to govern them. They are to be kept away from places of worship, as well as from bloodshed and prostitution.
verses.26: Then, Paul, taking those men with him on that day, went into the temple. He announced that the time for their purification from sin had arrived, until each of them could be forgiven.
verses.27: And when those seven days were about to end, the Jews from Asia watched him continue his prayers in the temple. They also laid their hands on him as an act of worship.
verses.28: Men of Israel, help! This man is someone who teaches everyone according to the laws and traditions of this place. He even brought Greeks into the temple and made this holy place sacred.
verses.29: For they had previously warned Trófimon Ephesian about being in the city with him. They said that Paul had taken him to the temple.
verses.30: The entire city was stirred up, and there was a large amount of support from the people. They took Paul outside the temple, and immediately the doors were locked.
verses.31: They also demanded that he be killed by the commander of the army, because Jerusalem was completely under their control.
verses.32: He, having brought his own soldiers and commanders with him, marched against them. But when they saw the general and the soldiers, they stopped attacking Paul.
verses.33: Then the khilnarch arrived, took him away, and ordered that he be held in custody. It was unclear who he was and what his role was.
verses.34: But others said something else in the crowd. Unable to hear what was said due to the noise, he was ordered to be taken into the area where the intervention would take place.
verses.35: And when it happened to those who were on the higher floors, he was thrown down by the soldiers due to the violence of the crowd.
verses.36: For the crowd of people kept shouting. “Let him go.”
verses.37: “I am about to intervene in this matter,” said Paul to the commander. “Is there anything I should say to you?” The commander replied, “Do you think I’m a Greek?”
verses.38: So, aren’t you the Egyptian who, back then, caused chaos and brought four thousand Sicarians into the desert?
verses.39: Paul said, “I am a man who is a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia. I am not a citizen of any city. But I ask you to allow me to speak to the people.”
verses.40: After he was allowed to do so, Paul stood on the steps and addressed the people with his hands. In a moment of silence, he spoke in Hebrew.
